newsitem.title: USA: South Dakota winter wheat crop nearly all headed.
newsitem.headline: South Dakota winter wheat crop nearly all headed.

text.p: The winter wheat crop was 99 percent headed as of Sunday and 74 percent of the crop was turning color, according to the South Dakota Agricultural Statistics Service.
Eight percent of the winter wheat crop was excellent, 52 percent good, 28 percent fair, 11 percent poor and one percent very poor.
Warm weather enabled crops to make good progress during the week and topsoil moisture levels were five percent surplus, 62 percent adequate, 27 percent short and six percent very short.
Spring wheat was six percent excellent, 55 percent good, 31 percent fair, five percent poor and three percent very poor.
The sunflower crop was 15 percent excellent, 57 percent good, 20 percent fair, seven percent poor and one percent very poor.
The first cutting of alfalfa was 96 percent complete and the second cutting was nine percent complete.
Range and pastures were in mostly fair to excellent condition and stock water supplies were three percent short, 89 percent adequate and eight percent surplus.
